tldr:
\emph{Sharp minimax testing of conditional density-effect homogeneity: a \(3/8\) propensity-information elbow on a bounded anisotropic density class.} For the causal estimand \(\Delta(P)=\|H_P\|_2\), we prove the uniform minimax testing rates
\[
 F_{\mathrm e}(n,
u)=n^{-2
u/(6
u+1)},\qquad
 F(n,
u)=\max\{F_{\mathrm e}(n,
u),n^{-8
u/(32
u+1)}\},
\]
with no logarithmic correction. The unique transition is \(
u=3/8\): unknown propensity costs a genuine polynomial factor above this boundary and only a bounded factor at or below it. Explicit tests have exact finite-sample full-null size at most \(1/10\), allowing an arbitrary nonzero homogeneous signed-density effect \(r_P\), and power at least \(4/5\) at the stated separations. Normalized same-class priors with deterministic separation give matching converses against every Borel randomized test. Finite computability means a finite exact-real arithmetic/comparison procedure, with supplied-function evaluation access in the supplied-propensity experiment. The printed \(c,C,n_0\) are explicit conservative constants. The class \(\mathcal M_
u\) is this note's new bounded one-dimensional anisotropic density benchmark, motivated by Jain--Luedtke; it is neither their published locally nonparametric model nor their conditional-no-effect null.
gap: The closest conditional distributional-effect test targets equality of conditional arm laws and provides fixed-discrepancy asymptotic calibration. Scalar CATE minimax results and regression quadratic-null tests do not determine information loss when growing outcome directions share a rough propensity under an arbitrary nonzero homogeneous signed-density effect.
fill: A uniform matched frontier would combine a total original-record full-null test, same-class normalized likelihood converses, and the supplied-propensity comparison. It would state attainable profile and outcome resolution for a prospective bounded one-coordinate wealth benchmark.
